metaData.title: Dialogue with Netlink CEO Liu Yu: The Satellite Communication Used by the 'Biao Ren' Crew, I Hope Most People Can Afford It Too | Diverse Companies
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article features an exclusive interview with Netlink CEO Liu Yu, exploring how satellite communication is shifting from B/G ends to C-end mass adoption, detailing product technology breakthroughs (miniaturized antennas, self-developed chips) and market strategies (segmented customer groups, scenario-driven), and using cases like the 'Biao Ren' crew to illustrate the civilian value of satellite communication.
metaData.summary: The article is an in-depth interview by ifanr with Netlink CEO Liu Yu. Netlink is a satellite communication terminal startup dedicated to pushing satellite communication from the B-end/G-end to the C-end market. Liu Yu elaborated on the timing of the startup, industry pain points, product philosophy, and technological breakthroughs. Netlink believes that China's satellite communication resources are being built at a high speed, but the lack of terminals and application ecosystems has led to an unclosed commercial loop. Drawing on their experience in the consumer electronics industry, the team defines products based on user needs, introducing precision manufacturing and industrial design into satellite terminals to achieve miniaturization, low cost, and mass production. Technical highlights include a miniaturized dual-motor transmission structure developed in collaboration with the MacBook hinge team, a self-developed GaN PA chip (reducing costs by three times while leading in performance), and edge computing and AI algorithms to optimize low-bandwidth video transmission. In terms of the market, Netlink focuses on scenario exploration, having provided communication support for the 'Biao Ren' crew in uninhabited areas and events like the 800 Li Desert Extreme Race, while also discovering the need for emergency communication in densely populated urban areas. Liu Yu believes the C-end satellite communication market requires patience, advocating for segmenting target customer groups more finely and gradually moving from prosumer C-end to the mass market, with an annual shipment of 100,000 units being a crucial threshold. The article demonstrates how entrepreneurs use consumer electronics thinking to transform a traditional industry, offering reference value for understanding the C-end landing of commercial aerospace.

mainPoints.point: The C-end transformation of satellite communication requires introducing consumer electronics methodologies (user insight, precision manufacturing) into the traditional industry.
mainPoints.explanation: The Netlink team comes from the consumer electronics industry, defining products based on user needs and tackling the pain points of satellite terminals being 'bulky, expensive, and hard to use' through hardware design, molds, and self-developed chips.

mainPoints.point: Build terminals rather than satellites, focus on 'value beyond connection', and solve low-bandwidth application issues through edge computing and AI.
mainPoints.explanation: Netlink does not build its own satellite network but focuses on the terminal and application layers, using edge computing and AI for video compression and frame interpolation in bandwidth-constrained scenarios to achieve high-definition transmission at extremely low bandwidth.

mainPoints.point: The C-end market requires gradual penetration from prosumer users, target customer groups must be segmented more finely, and an annual shipment of 100,000 units is an important threshold.
mainPoints.explanation: Netlink first serves prosumer C-end segments like uninhabited area off-road travel, film crews, and outdoor events, planning to push towards a broader mass market next, viewing an annual shipment of 100,000 units as the key step into a larger market.

mainPoints.point: Self-developing core chips is not only a cost-control measure but also the key to product definition rights.
mainPoints.explanation: The self-developed GaN PA chip enables the terminal to match the transmission power of large equipment despite its small size, ranking in the top three in the Ministry of Emergency Management's comparative tests, while reducing bare die costs by three times.

keyQuotes: Applying the mature 'user insight → requirement definition → technology implementation' methodology from the consumer electronics industry, along with precision manufacturing capabilities, to an industry that previously only talked about technical feasibility.

Internally, we talk about 'creating value beyond connection'; it's not just about solving the problem of whether communication works or not, but also diving deep into specific scenarios to optimize applications.
Our startup is about 'entering the narrow gate'; if it were a massive market right from the start, it wouldn't be our turn to start a business.
